r2_body: 1† Thou haſt broken the heads of the dragon : thou haſt giuen him for meate to the peoples of the Ethiopians.ak d. † Thou haſt broken vp fountanes, and torrentes: thou haſt dried the riuers of Ethan. geuem Materout of rockes, ſmade paſſage ouer Tordan. † The day is thine, and the night is thine : thou haſt made the morning and the ſunne. † Thou haſt made al the coaſts of the earth : the ſummer and the ſpring thou haſt formed them. † Be mindeful of this, the enimie hath vpbraided our Lord: and a fooliſh people hath prouoked thy name. † Deliuer not to beaſts the ſoules that confeſſe to thee : and the ſoules of thy poore forger not for euer. † Haue reſpect vnto thy teſtament : becauſe they that are obſcure of the earth, are filled with houſes of iniquities. Ignorant, blind, and barbarous infidels, lodge al kindes ofiniquitie in their conſciences † Ler not the humble be rurned away being confounded: the poore and needy shal praiſe thy name. v and therfore is is vnmeete, that faithful people ſhould he in bondage vnder them. † Ariſe God, iudge thy cauſe : be mindful of thoſe thy repro- ches, that are from the fooliſh man al the day. Theſe foolith audacious mem do continually bſaſtheme af holie thinges. †x Forget not the voices of thine enimies: the y pride of them that hate thee, hath aſcended alwaies. x Omie not to pxnith thum, yſeing iho are obſtinais and obduraie in pride, and hatred. Tbe wicked puie remarded. the 5.key. I Vnto the end, Corrupt not, a Pſalme of Canticle to Aſaph.
